questions.prompt: A VM now runs in the secondary region after a committed Site Recovery failover. You choose Re-Protect to prepare for returning to the primary. What does this do?

options.text: Immediately moves production execution to the primary.
options.explanation: Reprotection starts reverse replication; failback is a later recovery operation.

options.text: Deletes all backups in a Backup vault.
options.explanation: Site Recovery reprotection is not an Azure Backup deletion operation.

options.text: Keeps only primary-to-secondary replication without collecting secondary changes.
options.explanation: Returning safely requires replication of changes from the current secondary VM toward the primary.

options.text: Replicates from the secondary region toward the primary region.
options.explanation: This is the documented reverse replication direction after failover.

questions.prompt: A VM was failed over and reprotected from secondary to primary using Site Recovery. Before failback, which two checks are required by the tutorial?

options.text: The replicated VM is healthy/protected and synchronization is complete.
options.explanation: Failback should use a healthy, synchronized replicated item.

options.text: The original primary VM is powered on to receive disk changes.
options.explanation: The tutorial requires the original primary-region VM to be shut down; an active VM can make failback fail.

options.text: The primary region is available and required resource access is permitted.
options.explanation: Availability and resource permissions are prerequisites for returning to that region.

options.text: All replication recovery points are deleted before the failback starts.
options.explanation: Failback uses a selected recovery point; deleting them beforehand is not a prerequisite.

questions.prompt: A Site Recovery failback has returned your VM to the primary region. What restores disaster recovery coverage toward the secondary region?

options.text: Assume protection has resumed without checking replication.
options.explanation: The tutorial calls for reprotection after failback.

options.text: Reprotect the primary VM toward the secondary and verify replication health.
options.explanation: This restores the intended primary-to-secondary replication direction.

options.text: Leave reverse replication permanently configured toward the primary.
options.explanation: Once execution is primary again, the intended recovery destination is the secondary.

options.text: Run Cleanup test failover instead of reprotection.
options.explanation: Test-drill cleanup is a separate workflow and does not establish production replication.
